summary: Allison Thackston's guide explains how to set up a ROS2 development environment using VSCode and Docker, aimed at developers familiar with coding but maybe not ROS. It covers the base and development ROS2 Docker images, a folder structure, a .devcontainer config with Dockerfile and extensions, C++ IntelliSense settings, colcon build and test tasks, and launch configurations for Python and C++ gdb debugging. The page is a clipped blog post with navigation and related-post boilerplate, which was ignored.
one_line: A guide by Allison Thackston to setting up ROS2 development in VSCode using Docker dev containers, with tasks and debugger configuration.
key_facts: The guide is written by Allison Thackston and dated Dec 29, 2019.
The guide is intended for people familiar with coding and software development but maybe not ROS.
ROS2 is described as the next generation of software libraries for robotics development.
The author maintains ROS2 Docker images on dockerhub under althack/ros2, with a base version and a development version.
The base ROS2 image has the minimal dependencies needed to run ROS2 and is suited to deploying code without writing new code.
The development image is based on the base version and adds the dependencies needed to compile and create new packages.
The recommended folder structure places .devcontainer, .vscode and src directories in the folder opened in VSCode, with ROS2 packages inside src.
The example Dockerfile starts with FROM althack/ros2:foxy-dev.
The devcontainer.json sets remoteUser to "ros" and runArgs include --cap-add=SYS_PTRACE and --security-opt seccomp=unconfined to support gdb debugging.
The c_cpp_properties.json includes /opt/ros/foxy/include and uses cppStandard c++17 with cStandard c11.
The tasks.json defines a build task running colcon build with -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug and a test task running colcon test && colcon test-result.
The C++ gdb launch configuration uses type cppdbg with MIMode gdb and prompts for package and program names via inputs.
The Python launch configuration uses type python with program set to ${file} and console set to integratedTerminal.
The recommended devcontainer extensions include ms-iot.vscode-ros, ms-vscode.cpptools, ms-python.python and ms-azuretools.vscode-docker.
